title: Sipser-Spielman meets Dijkgraaf-Witten: non-Abelian qLDPC codes via twisted sheaf gauge theory and almost-constant-overhead magic state fountain
authors: Guanyu Zhu, Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin
abstract: Sipser-Spielman codes and Dijkgraaf-Witten twisted gauge theories are among the most profound ideas in the last few decades in the areas of computer science and mathematical physics respectively. This work unifies them in the same framework using the language of sheaf cohomology, and produces a new framework of twisted sheaf guage theories describing a class of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with non-Abelian $D_4$ topological order. The corresponding twisted qLDPC code can be obtained from gauging a new type of 0-form sub-complex $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ symmetry from a qLDPC code defined on a sheaf complex, and can be interpreted as a topological defect network of non-Abelain $D_4$ patches glued together with proper gapped interfaces. As an application, one can use this to realize a \textit{magic state fountain} via the gauging measurement of the addressable logical CZ gates as 0-form subcomplex symmetries in a 2D hypergraph-product on a sheaf complex. This includes a scheme of subdividing an arbitrary constant-rate 2D hypergraph-product code with parameter $[[n,Θ(n), Ω(n^{1/2})]]$ into a quantum sheaf code which allows preparation of $Θ(n^{1/2})$ in parallel, equivalent to the recent geometric construction using the code-to-manifold mapping in (arXiv:2601.06736). Moreover, using the recent sheaf complex and algebraic code constructions by Golowich-Tamo-Zhu (arXiv:2609.27801) with parameter $[[n,Θ(n^{1-ε}), Ω(n^{(1-ε)/2})]]$ for arbitrary small $ε$, one can prepare $Θ(n^{1-ε})$ CZ magic states in parallel and hence achieve an almost-constant magic rate.
summary: This work merges concepts from coding theory (Sipser-Spielman) and topological field theory (Dijkgraaf-Witten) using sheaf cohomology to define novel non-Abelian qLDPC codes. These codes possess non-Abelian D4 topological order and are shown to enable the efficient preparation of magic states, crucial for scaling quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper unifies Sipser-Spielman codes and Dijkgraaf-Witten twisted gauge theories to construct a new framework for non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes.
main_result: This framework yields qLDPC codes with non-Abelian D4 topological order and provides a method to realize a magic state fountain achieving an almost-constant magic rate.
method: The construction relies on sheaf cohomology to define the code by gauging a specific 0-form sub-complex symmetry within a sheaf complex structure.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum error-correcting codes (qLDPC) exhibiting non-Abelian D4 topological order, analyzed using sheaf gauge theory on complex structures.
key_observables: The magic state rate (aiming for almost-constant overhead) and the topological order (non-Abelian D4).
important_parameters: Code parameters like $[[n, \Theta(n), \Omega(n^{1/2})]]$ and the field structure $\mathbb{F}_q$.
main_assumptions: The work assumes the validity of using sheaf cohomology to bridge coding theory and topological field theory concepts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the subdivision process of codes, the structure of transversal CZ gates labeled by sheaf 0-cocycles, and the path integral representation as a slab of twisted theory.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first unifying the theoretical concepts, then detailing the construction of the qLDPC code via gauging symmetries, and finally applying this to the realization of magic state fountains and achieving improved magic state rates.
why_interesting: It provides a deep mathematical connection between topological order, algebraic coding theory, and quantum resource generation (magic states), which is fundamental to fault-tolerant quantum computation.
